articles.title: Presidente de Paraguay no acude al Senado y delega a sus abogados para presentar defensa
articles.summary: Santiago Peña deberá acudir al Senado paraguayo para ejercer su defensa en el proceso de juicio político, luego de que rechazaran su pedido de más tiempo.
articles.body_text: Los abogados del presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, acudieron este viernes al Senado para presentar la defensa “técnica” y “jurídica” del mandatario en el juicio político iniciado en su contra, que, pese a haber sido convocado en persona para comparecer ante el Legislativo, no asistió y delegó por ahora su representación, en medio del escándalo desatado por el cierre del privado Ueno Bank. Los letrados, Adolfo Ferreiro y Ricardo Preda, llegaron al pleno cerca de las 13.00 horas locales (16.00 GMT) y tras el rechazo del Senado al pedido de prórroga de 72 horas solicitado por Peña para ejercer su defensa. Peña, quien permanece formalmente en el cargo después de que el Congreso no se pronunció por falta de cuórum sobre la renuncia que presentó la víspera, había advertido poco antes que las 12 horas establecidas por el Senado para preparar su estrategia eran insuficientes. Paraguay atraviesa por una crisis política después de que el Banco Central (BCP) ordenó un proceso de resolución o cierre de Ueno bank, una institución que durante la gestión de Peña recibió millonarios recursos de entidades públicas. El BCP detectó que el índice de solvencia del banco, que controlaba los recursos de más de 2,9 millones de clientes, había caído por debajo del 50 % del mínimo exigido, “como consecuencia de ajustes realizados a sus estados financieros durante el proceso de regularización”. El jefe de Estado, señalado por sus vínculos con Ueno, terminó salpicado por la crisis y la víspera dimitió. Sin embargo, Peña permanece formalmente en la Presidencia de Paraguay ya que legisladores oficialistas dejaron sin cuórum la sesión conjunta convocada para votar su renuncia y así poder activar el mecanismo de sucesión tras declarar la vacancia del cargo. Si fuera destituido por el Parlamento, Peña perdería los fueros de senador vitalicio, que conservaría con la renuncia. Precisamente eso es lo que no quiere el Congreso, que lo convocó de manera inmediata al Senado, que actúa como juez, para el juicio político en el que está previsto que lo destituya.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Sequoia shutting down its Scouts program marks the end of an era | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sequoia pioneered the scouts model and many VC firms followed suit, but a consensus now seems to be forming that the model has reached limits in its current form.
articles.body_text: Sequoia this week announced a broad overhaul in a memo posted to X, a move that includes closing its London office and shutting down its scout program. Observers warn that it would be a mistake to read too much into the London closure, since the British capital has a thriving AI scene. On the other hand, the decision to end scouts says more about where venture investing is headed. That’s partly because 17 years ago, Sequoia pioneered the scouts model, in which select founders and operators write checks on the firm’s behalf. Amid increased competition for deal flow, many VC firms followed suit . But a consensus now seems to be emerging that the model has reached its limits in its current form. Not everyone was sold on the model in the first place. “They pioneered the scout program but [to be honest] it never made sense to me!” VC Sheel Mohnot wrote on X this week. “The scouts themselves don’t really care that much about the investments, you can still miss (like they did with Uber), not sure what it gets you. I suspect other firms will shutter theirs too,” he added. To be clear, Sequoia didn’t make a case against scouts in the memo. Instead, it framed its decision as part of a broader need for more focus. But its goal of “putting more energy behind fewer people and things” is likely to resonate with others who’ve questioned the ‘spray and pray’ approach to scouting. Rival firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), for instance, rolled out a global scout network aimed at spotting opportunities in the U.S. and also in smaller European hubs. But a16z partner Gabriel Vasquez told TechCrunch earlier this year that the firm had revamped its program to double down “on the best people.” Under this new approach, Vasquez explained, scouts get more resources but are also expected to be more active, such as by co-hosting dinners with the firm. “They get more budget, but we have reduced the number,” he said. This also seems to indicate that it is VC firms that have been driving an overhaul of the model. For founders, being a scout is attractive: it brings them closer to firms they may want checks from someday, or even a partner role with, and being seen as someone who can write a check can raise their standing among other founders. Some scouts will undoubtedly mourn the end of Sequoia’s program. Among them is Station F boss Roxanne Varza, who wrote on LinkedIn that she was “sad” to hear that the program was getting cut off, and “hope[d] that other funds [w]on’t follow suit.” Varza, a former Sequoia scout from 2020 to 2025, told TechCrunch that she had no information beyond what has been shared publicly, but observed that becoming a scout had often been a stepping stone for aspiring investment managers. “I cannot name all of the incredible scouts that have gone on to join or build funds, but there are quite a few. And the scout programs may have helped them get there — allowed them to build an investment track record, allowed them to build relationships with various funds directly, and more,” she wrote to TechCrunch. According to Varza, the program’s impact went beyond the individual level, instead helping the entire ecosystem become more mature. “I believe they have helped to foster the investment culture and early-stage investment landscape that we now see in Europe, for example,” Varza said. While others may agree with Varza about the role these programs have played, they may still have run their course for two reasons. First, seasoned operators may get more financial upside as angels. When it’s their own money, they get to keep the returns, too. Second, leading VC firms are now big and well-known enough that the best founders tend to come to them, so they worry less about missing deals, except at the very earliest stages or in niches and geographies where they have less reach.

articles.title: From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech | TechCrunch
articles.summary: After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the markets are about to do.
articles.body_text: Right before the midterm elections, OpenAI hired Jessica Schumer , daughter of Democratic Sen. Chuck Schumer. The company also said it would start calling its data centers “ compute campuses .” For the past two years, many of Silicon Valley’s biggest names have built closer ties with President Donald Trump and his administration. Several attended White House events, some companies scaled back diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and some executives donated millions to super PACs supporting his campaign and allied candidates. Administration policies also benefited the industry, including tax breaks, the pausing of some federal investigations, and looser AI regulation. Meanwhile, Meta faced lawsuits and billion-dollar fines, and OpenAI faced suits alleging its technology harmed users. Now, with the midterms shifting the balance of power in Washington, those same companies are working to rebuild ties with Democrats, who have pledged to tighten oversight of AI. How far that gets them may depend less on image-polishing than on where the real fights are happening: in state capitols, in communities deciding whether to host data centers, and, as we’ve seen this past week, in the markets watching the AI boom. J.B. Branch, director of federal AI governance and technology policy at Public Citizen, a nonprofit advocacy group that describes itself as nonpartisan, told me that the tech industry “realizes they have an optics problem.” He characterized moves like the Schumer hire and the rebranding as “PR washing.” He expects more of it, too, pointing to OpenAI’s partnership with the American Federation of Teachers, announced last year, as well as Anthropic’s newly launched Claude Corps and Meta’s America’s Workforce Academy. “I would imagine more of that sort of investment in these corporate, private-public partnerships,” he said. These initiatives didn’t spring up overnight. Meta and other tech companies reportedly began looking for ways to strengthen their ties to Democrats as Democratic gains in the midterms looked more likely. Reached for comment about the midterm elections’ impact on Meta, a company spokesperson pointed TechCrunch to remarks that Meta President Dina Powell McCormick made this week at WSJ Tech. “You have to work with the government that the American people elect,” McCormick had said. “I have seen it across the board that you have to be bipartisan, and you want to be, because you want buy-in on the things that you’re trying to do.” Not everyone expects them to work. Alice Marwick, director of research at the tech policy nonprofit Data & Society, told me she expects Big Tech to try to pivot back toward the middle, “if not the left. But it’s a little too late,” she said. “Tech companies should be asking themselves how their products can make people’s lives better, because right now, it doesn’t seem like they are.” If Democrats follow through on pledges to tighten oversight of AI and Big Tech, the industry could face a tougher environment. Data center moratoriums are gaining traction, and a wave of AI regulation bills awaits drafting. At the same event, Powell McCormick said Meta wants to show that communities welcoming its investments will see “an enormous amount of benefit,” while those that don’t want them “will of course have the right to stop them.” Still, the next two years could bring political gridlock in Washington. Aryan Ranjan, founder of Baraza, a political campaign management software company, told me most action will likely happen at the state level, since states have already sued tech companies and passed regulations. “A coalition built on newer, working-class voters is likely to push Democrats to frame AI around electricity bills, data-center siting and jobs rather than abstract AI safety,” he said of what to expect at the federal level. Last December, the Trump administration signed an executive order creating the AI Litigation Task Force , a federal group meant to challenge state AI laws. The administration has argued that U.S. AI companies “must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulations.” Many states have nonetheless passed their own laws, including measures on chatbots and deepfakes. It also remains to be seen how President Trump will respond, including whether he’ll sign more AI executive orders or veto bills that could be seen as anti-AI. Clearly, voters want stronger guardrails around the technology. In a statement to TechCrunch, a White House official said: “American leadership in super intelligence is essential for our national security, economic prosperity, and the quality of life of the American people. President Trump is committed to ensuring America continues to lead the world in super intelligence while protecting American consumers. As the President has said, he’s willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.” Branch argued that Trump’s political fortunes are now tied to the AI industry. On Wednesday, the day after the midterms, a trillion-dollar market sell-off spooked investors, some are whom are reportedly now reconsidering Anthropic’s reported trillion-dollar IPO. “There’s a very strong likelihood that there will be an AI bubble pop, and it’ll happen on Trump’s hands,” Branch said, predicting a possible market collapse. “Does he want to sink or swim along with the AI industry?”

articles.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
articles.body_text: Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion , confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management. Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, but it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus. The deal highlights how difficult it can be for independent data center developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power. Growing opposition from local communities can further complicate development. Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn’t walked away from working with Crusoe entirely. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. The deal to sell the site to Google was first reported by Bloomberg in June, but the Wyoming setback didn’t stop Crusoe from raising a $3.9 billion round in September. Crusoe makes money by leasing data center space to customers that bring their own GPUs, by renting out its own GPUs, and by selling compute power used to run AI models, known as inference. Crusoe’s largest projects serve some of the biggest names in AI. Its campus in Abilene, Texas, is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and the company is also constructing a separate 900-megawatt campus next door for Microsoft, with its first building expected to come online in mid-2027. Meta is also a customer, and Bloomberg reported that the trading firm Jane Street signed a $13 billion , five-year cloud deal with Crusoe. Crusoe was founded by Chase Lochmiller, now its CEO, and Cully Cavness, who started it as a cryptocurrency-mining business powered by natural gas that would otherwise have been burned off. In September, alongside its $3.9 billion funding round, the company added three board members , including JB Straubel, the Redwood Materials founder and Tesla board member who invested in Crusoe in 2021. articles.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.
articles.body_text: OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion. Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg. In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target. TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds. The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted. Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago. OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans. There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point. The market for AI hangs in a particularly precarious place. The Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterms — and overwhelmingly negative voter sentiment around data centers — has caused jitters throughout the market , with many anticipating potential regulatory challenges in the future. articles.title: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple | TechCrunch
articles.summary: There are now 100,000 Duo-optimized apps, says Apple, and thousands more arrive daily.
articles.body_text: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch. But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front. The company on Friday announced there are now over 100,000 apps built for the Duo live on the App Store, and it’s seeing thousands more being added to the store every day. The news was timed alongside the release of over a dozen more notable Duo-ready apps, including Microsoft Word and Outlook, Zoom, sports apps from the NBA and NHL, shopping apps like Etsy and LTK, productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra, the Halide Mark III camera app, and others. These join the iPhone Duo-optimized apps that were already available, like Netflix, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Non-optimized apps are definitely less than ideal, as they come with a black bar on the side of the screen, which takes up valuable space. Sometimes, they hide important functions under an overflow menu. Apple’s data seems to suggest that at least some iOS developers may have needed extra time to get their apps ready for its latest form factor. The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide. Here, the developers could use the Duo and work on their apps with Apple’s support. The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year. On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve . “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added. Other notable apps that have been updated for iOS 27 and optimized for the iPhone Duo include the following: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (U.K.), Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer, Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, FOX News, Kalshi, Yahoo Finance, Canva, Suno, Tinder, Google Translate, Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel, Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline, Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd, The Weather Channel, FOX Weather, and RainViewer. Not all these updates have yet to fully roll out, we should note. Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo. articles.title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.
articles.body_text: Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers. Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them. As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent. Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf. For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab. Or, if you’re focused on collecting recipes for an upcoming family event, you’d open a new Space for that particular project. Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects. “Describe an idea in chat, and Muse builds a space for you, whether that’s a tracker, a planner or a project board,” Meta says. Spaces can also be easily integrated with third-party apps and information, Meta says. “Connect the apps you use, and your spaces keep themselves up to date in the background, so new concert dates, price changes, or savings progress show up without you having to ask,” the company says. On Friday, Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s founder and CEO, posted about the new feature on X: “Playing around with spaces in Muse lately — tell Muse what you need and it builds it. I’ve made a BBQ game, an event tracker, and a home control dashboard. Excited to see what you build.” Muse agents — and the cuddly avatars that enclose them — have been greeted with a relatively warm reception over the past few months. During its earnings call in October, Zuckerberg said that its agents had 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada — less than two months after the agents debuted. The company is obviously busy building out the user experience around the agents. Spaces is actually the second new Muse feature that Meta has debuted over the last week. On Thursday, the company also announced Muse Voice , which allows users to video chat with their agent and give it commands verbally. The company is in competition with other cute and cuddly AI agents — including OpenAI’s dots and SpaceXAI’s Grokbot , which were debuted with similarly cartoonish personas. articles.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
articles.body_text: Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it. A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month. As Anthropic gears up for its IPO , the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed. “Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.” Kharazian said he’s already seeing evidence that the top 1% of firms — the most “ AI-pilled ” — have stuttered slightly in their spend in August and September, coming up just below the $10,000 per-employee they were hitting at their summer peaks. A slowdown among that cohort is “sufficient to slow down revenue entirely, despite the fact that we’re seeing rising volumes,” he said. Ramp data shows growth in spending among median and top 10%, but it’s not enough to make up the difference. Median firms spend $12-$15 per employee per month, and the top 10% spend $600-$1,000. “If you look at the use cases today, it’s not necessarily clear they will get up to that $10,000 per employee per month mark that the 1% is at,” Kharazian said. While there’s plenty of demand for AI coding agents in industries like software and finance, “it’s not necessarily true that a doctor’s office or a car dealership will need to spend that much on AI.” “The era of hypergrowth may be over, and now that we know there may not be as much juice to squeeze out of the top 1%,” he continued. October data did see a re-acceleration, with token spend up 8.9% from September 23 to October 23, but Kharazian said the headwinds on spend growth are strong. Kharazian (who has published a series of blogs called “ Cracks in the AI Thesis ”) said the slowdown isn’t due to a demand problem. Again, AI volumes are up. Instead he points to the competitive nature of the marketplace. “OpenAI and Anthropic price cuts have…just made it cheaper to use AI,” he said. In September, OpenAI cut API prices in half for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Answering the price war, Anthropic has also made significant reductions to pricing for Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 — a decision that the company said in a recent filing slashed revenue growth by about $600 million. Both companies have also been offering enterprise discounts that are intended to lock-in spend, but in reality are hitting their revenue targets. Kharazian said this dynamic means it has very much become a buyer’s market.

articles.title: After blocking Muse, Amazon now lets users text Alexa to help them shop | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon said that the feature will roll out to millions of users in coming weeks.
articles.body_text: Amazon is jumping on the currently most popular bandwagon for interacting with AI agents: texting. The company on Friday said it is launching a feature that lets customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to help them shop, much like you can with AI agents like Muse or Instinct. The move comes after Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse from querying its site in September. The company is rolling the features out just before the start of the holiday shopping season. The e-commerce giant said select U.S. customers will get a text asking them to enable the shopping feature. Those with access can text Alexa to shop on Amazon using natural language queries, spanning everything from searching for items, adding them to cart, and purchasing. The text agent builds on the recent shopping-focused upgrades to Alexa , and so can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products, and check the status of orders. Users can also share a picture of an item or someone wearing an outfit to search for similar listings on Amazon. The company said over time, Alexa will learn users’ preferences and suggest items accordingly. As the market for consumer-focused AI agents balloons, platforms like Amazon are building their own to tap this new avenue of user interaction. Last month, delivery company DoorDash said that third-party agents had so far only placed hundreds of orders in total on its platform, and that it plans to concentrate on developing its own text-based agent, launched in September , further. articles.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The decision to wind down the EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. Elon Musk said the company will use the factory space to make more Cybercabs.
articles.body_text: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis. The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years. Tesla is killing off the Cybertruck at a moment when it is trying to become an AI- and robotics-focused company. A big part of that is its robotaxi ambitions. The company has spent the last two months putting Cybercabs on the streets in its hometown of Austin, Texas. With no major incidents to date, the company has said it plans to expand the Cybercabs operations to other cities, starting with Dallas later this month. (Tesla also operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUVs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas, as well as three cities in Florida.) This is the third product Tesla has discontinued in order to fuel those greater ambitions. Earlier this year, the company decided to end production of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV and instead use the factory space dedicated to those vehicles to make Optimus humanoid robots. First announced in 2019, the Cybertruck was a product that Musk had long obsessed over. “Probably my personal favorite for the next product is the pickup truck, and we are going to just do an amazing pickup truck,” he said on one of Tesla’s earnings calls that year. Musk promised the Cybertruck would be radical, inspired by the designs of cyberpunk sci-fi stories like “Blade Runner.” While that certainly bore out in the design, the company overpromised on the basics of the Cybertruck from the jump. During the now-infamous reveal event in 2019, when head designer Franz von Holzhausen cracked the Cybertruck’s windows with steel balls, Tesla said the EV was supposed to start at under $40,000 and have up to 500 miles of range. It achieved neither of those figures. Instead, the truck was delayed for two years, in part because of the COVID-19 pandemic. When it finally did hit the market in late 2023, Tesla handed over the first few Cybertrucks to customers in a short, somewhat odd for Tesla event (by the company’s own standards, at least), which saw a poorly-lit Musk standing in a truck bed promising the truck was “the finest in apocalyptic equipment” fit for “late civilization vibes.” The base price had inflated to around $60,000, and the top-end range had shrunk by over 100 miles. The truck has struggled on the market ever since. The polarizing design never seemed to sit well with buyers, especially at a higher-than-expected price. Then, during its first full year of sales in 2024, Musk became a major financial backer of Donald Trump, which turned the instantly recognizable Cybertruck into a target for protesters. That continued into 2025 as Musk led the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, which fired thousands of federal workers. articles.title: At least 10 local governments have moved to drop Flock’s surveillance cameras since summer | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The concerns range from privacy to how data is shared (and with whom) to procurement concerns.
articles.body_text: Flock, founded in 2017, sells surveillance software that can help solve crimes, such as finding missing people or stolen cars. Its products include license plate readers, drones, and microphone-based edge-computing devices to pick up gunshots and other sounds. More than 100,000 Flock cameras are in use nationwide. But in the past three months, Monroe , Ohio; Newburgh , New York; Richmond , Virginia; Hopkinton, Massachusetts; New Bedford , Massachusetts; and Lansing , Michigan, have all moved to end their contracts with Flock. Meanwhile, police in East Bridgewater and Grafton, Massachusetts, also announced plans to stop using Flock cameras. Just this week, residents of League City, Texas, voted against their police department’s continued use of Flock’s license plate readers, and the cameras are now set to be removed. In Asheville, North Carolina, police lost access to Flock after the city voted to terminate its contract in August, and the El Paso County Sheriff’s Office in Colorado announced in September that it would stop using Flock cameras. When asked for comment, the El Paso County Sheriff’s Office redirected TechCrunch to its press release, where Sheriff Joseph Roybal said that discontinuing the use of Flock was the right decision for the county. “We have the tools, training, and experience to locate and apprehend criminals without relying on Flock cameras,” he said in the press release. Misuse has been a real problem. In August, for example, an officer in Brentwood, Missouri was accused of using Flock cameras to stalk his ex-wife during their divorce. In September, an officer from East Texas was sentenced to prison for using Flock to stalk his ex-girlfriend and her family. Another growing concern is how immigration officials have been able to access the technology. One case that captures the issue came in March, when Ithaca, New York, passed a resolution to terminate its contract with the Flock Group. In the resolution, the city said there were “proven instances of Flock Safety infrastructure being used by federal agents for information purposes even without specific authorizations from the contracting locality,” and that the city had reviewed reports that “either intentionally or through its negligence,” Flock had allowed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) to “use query results from its database of state and local ALPR [automatic license plate reader] data to investigate and persecute immigrants throughout the United States.” “Every day, police departments across the country are using Flock technology to solve serious crimes, locate suspects, find missing people, and make a measurable impact on public safety,” Flock told TechCrunch in a statement. “While we respect every community’s decision, removing a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes and protect communities moves public safety backward. Every Flock customer owns its data and controls who it is shared with and how it can be used. Flock does not sell data and does not have a contract with ICE.” This August, Flock announced it would shorten the default period it stores data for new customers, from 30 days to seven. It also said agencies now need a case code before they can search the database. That lack of awareness is similar to how data centers are popping up across the country, often before residents understand what is happening. Schwartz said police departments often decide to use Flock on their own, with little oversight from city councils. In South Windsor , Connecticut, according to local reports, Flock cameras went live last year without public warning or a vote. In October, the town voted to remove its Flock cameras. “Grassroots activists across the country have been demanding that city councils exercise their procurement power to refuse to pay for ALPRs,” Schwartz said, referring to councils’ power to decide what the city buys. He added that activists have been fighting for years and that “many city councils are listening.” The main argument for technology like Flock is that it helps combat crime and keep neighborhoods safe. And many local governments are not dropping Flock or similar technology; instead, they are adding restrictions on its use or looking for alternatives.

articles.title: The Moto Tag is an AirTag for Android
articles.summary: Motorola is introducing a new tracker called the Moto Tag that is compatible with Google’s Find My Device network and has UWB. It’s basically an AirTag, but for Android.
articles.body_text: Motorola’s tracking tag is officially here, and if you’ve wanted an AirTag for your Android phone, this new Moto Tag might be it. This item tracker costs $29 and works with Google’s newly upgraded Find My Device network to help you locate a lost item. In addition to Bluetooth, it also offers ultra wideband, which means that if your phone is equipped with a UWB chip — like the Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra — you can track down the tag’s precise location. You know, just like you can with an AirTag. The Moto Tag comes with an IP67 rating, so it should survive a dunk in fresh water. The tag is powered by a CR2032 coin cell battery and should last a full year before it needs a new one. And in the event that you have your tag on hand but can’t find your phone, pressing a button on the Moto Tag will ring your phone to help you find it. The multifunction button can also be used as a remote shutter for your Motorola phone’s camera. articles.title: 3D DRAM created by IBM and Micron, 128GBps memory on the way
articles.summary: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GB transfer speed scould be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron, using stacked chips and TSVs.
articles.body_text: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GBps transfer speeds could be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron. The companies have developed three-dimensional memory, stacking individual DRAM chips vertically that would normally have to be placed side-by-side, though the efficiencies gained aren’t solely down to space. Communication between the stacked chips and the host device is achieved through a new creation known as through-silicon vias, or TSVs, which run vertically through the pile of chips and act as conduits to the host device. Thanks to the TSVs, in testing the memory has reached data speeds of 128GBps, ten times faster than current memory. On top of this, IBM claims the chips are 70 percent more power efficient than today’s DRAM. The new research is expected to form a key part of Samsung and Micron’s Hybrid Memory Cube technology, first announced back in October. IBM and Micron hope to have commercial availability in two years, with servers likely to use it first. Looking beyond that, IBM fellow Subu Iyer said that the new process “will have applications beyond memory, enabling other industry segments as well.” What exactly those new segments are remains to be seen, but we certainly wouldn’t complain if our computers got the kind of speed bump described here.

articles.title: Gabrielsson: ”Förstår oron och besvikelsen”
articles.summary: Fredagens besked från SD, C och M har förändrat spelplanen i regeringsbildningen. V-toppen Ida Gabrielsson säger att hon ”förstår oron och besvikelsen” – efter Centerpartiets öppning för en borgerlig regering. ”V önskar att vi rödgröna gjort mer”, skriver hon på Facebook.
articles.body_text: Fredagens besked från SD, C och M har förändrat spelplanen i regeringsbildningen. V-toppen Ida Gabrielsson säger att hon ”förstår oron och besvikelsen” – efter Centerpartiets öppning för en borgerlig regering. ”V önskar att vi rödgröna gjort mer”, skriver hon på Facebook. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På fredagen meddelade SD att partiet kan acceptera en borgerlig fyrpartiregering som man självt inte ingår i – och öppnade därmed dörren för Centerpartiet. Centerpartiets Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist höll senare på eftermiddagen en pressträff där hon begärde in varsitt totalpaket från både Magdalena Andersson (S) och Ulf Kristersson (M). I paketen de ska förklara vilken slags regering de ser framför sig och vilken politik de vill föra. I ett långt inlägg på Facebook kommenterar Vänsterpartiets viceordförande Ida Gabrielsson det nya läget. ” Givetvis hoppas jag att C återgår till den positionen dom haft tidigare, dvs står fast vid att de inte låter sig väljas på SD-mandat, och därmed göra sig helt SD-beroende. V inser att det inte blir en total ”vänstersväng” eftersom C:s mandat också kommer att behövas och det har vi också varit tydliga med i våra samtal. ” Centerpartiets öppning har rört upp känslor i det rödgröna lägret. Gabrielsson skriver att hon förstår besvikelsen över utvecklingen. ” Jag förstår oron och besvikelsen som vi är många som känner. V önskar att vi rödgröna gjort mer tillsammans för att C tydligare skulle ha valt det rödgröna regeringsunderlaget innan valet, så att väljare som röstade för att byta ut Tidö visste vad dom röstade på. ” Gabrielsson varnar även Centerpartiet för efterspelet som skulle följa på ett sidbyte från Andersson till Kristersson.

articles.title: JUST NU: Fem döda i skjutning
articles.summary: Fem personer har dödats och ett dussintal skadats i en skjutning på ett torg i centrala Krakow. Skotten avlossades från en förbipasserande bil. Skytten, som bar militärkläder, sköts av polis.
articles.body_text: Fem personer har dödats och ett dussintal skadats i en skjutning på ett torg i centrala Krakow. Skotten avlossades från en förbipasserande bil. Skytten, som bar militärkläder, sköts av polis. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Flera personer har skjutits på torget Rynek Glowny i centrala Krakow . Enligt polsk polis har fem personer dödats och ett dussintal skadats. Skotten avlossades från en bil. Polisen säger i ett uttalande: ”En man som hade kört in på torget började skjuta mot slumpmässigt utvalda personer från sin bil. Gärningsmannen har gripits. Flera personer har skadats, däribland poliser.” I videor på sociala medier syns en polisbil följa efter en mörk bil som kör i riktning mot torget. Höga smällar hörs och människor flyr. Daniel Schatz, frilansskribent och debattör, befann sig på torget. – Jag hörde att skott avlossades och såg att någon föll ihop. Jag antar att det är en av de skjutna. Då började jag förflytta mig rätt snabbt från området. Nu är det kaos. Det fullt av poliser och personal från räddningstjänsten, och stora avspärrningar. – Nej, jag tror att det tog lång tid innan polisen anlände. Jag tror folk inte riktigt reagerade. Nu rapporterar man om minst fem döda och att skjutningen skedde från en bil. Om man tittar på videor i sociala medier ser man en man i militärmundering, men det såg jag inte. Polisen bekräftar att skytten var bar militärkläder och uppger att han använde ett längre militärgevär vid skjutningen. Han sköts av polis och fördes sedan till sjukhus.

articles.title: Marius överfallen i sitt hem

articles.body_text: Bonusprinsen Marius Borg Høiby överfölls i sitt hem på Skaugum på fredagen. Norska Se og Hør skriver att en man sparkade på dörren och knuffade Borg Høiby. Kungaparet ska ha varit hemma när händelsen inträffade. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Marius Borg Høiby lyssnade på musik och målade när han på fredagskvällen hörde ett bankande på dörren, enligt Se og Hør. En förvirrad Marius öppnade dörren för att ta reda på vad som pågick. Då ska en okänd man ha trängt sig förbi honom och in i huset på Skaugum, där han sitter i häktad. Mannen ska ha knuffat Marius innan han tvingades ut ur huset. Den norska säkerhetspolisen PST bekräftar för Dagbladet att en person gripits i närheten av bostaden. – PST kan bekräfta att våra besättningar grep en person nära Høibys bostad. Utöver det har vi ingen kommentar, säger Eirik Veum på PST till tidningen. Enligt Se og Hør var kung Haakon och drottning Mette-Marit hemma vid tidpunkten, men inte i samma hus. – Det är uppenbarligen mycket allvarligt och mycket obehagligt att få besök i sitt eget hem. Det är en plats där man ska känna sig trygg, och i den situation Marius befinner sig i just nu är det lätt att förstå att han har upplevt detta som mycket obehagligt och osäkert, säger Borg Høibys advokat Alexander Greaker till tidningen. Tidigare i veckan beslutade en domare att Borg Høiby fortsatt måste bära fotboja på det kungliga godset Skaugum.

articles.title: Maud Olofssons varning efter SD:s besked: ”Äta upp”
articles.summary: SD går i opposition men kan släppa fram en borgerlig regering. Den tidigare C-ledaren Maud Olofsson säger i en kommentar till Expressen att SD vill ”äta upp” S. ”S är det parti som SD gillar allra minst och där SD:s långsiktiga mål har varit att försvaga det partiet”.
articles.body_text: SD går i opposition men kan släppa fram en borgerlig regering. Den tidigare C-ledaren Maud Olofsson säger i en kommentar till Expressen att SD vill ”äta upp” S. ”S är det parti som SD gillar allra minst och där SD:s långsiktiga mål har varit att försvaga det partiet”. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Sverigedemokraterna går i opposition men kan släppa fram en borgerlig fyrpartiregering, meddelade partiledaren Jimmie Åkesson vid lunchtid på fredagen. Ett par timmar senare höll Centerpartiets ledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist en pressträff och uppmanade de båda statsministerkandidaterna, Socialdemokraternas ledare Magdalena Andersson och Moderaternas ledare Ulf Kristersson, att presentera ”totalpaket” för hur de vill styra Sverige och med vilka partier. De ombads också att redogöra för hur de ska minimera inflytandet för Vänsterpartiet och Sverigedemokraterna. C-kännare menar att partiet nu har ett drömläge som vågmästare. Den före detta C-ledaren Maud Olofsson skriver i en kommentar till Expressen att SD:s drag ”var mycket väntat”. ”Min analys är att SD håller på att fundera över sin strategi framåt och då bedömer man ju att oppositionspositionen tjänar dom bäst. Det innebär också att de skulle tjäna väldigt lite på att vara konstruktiva gentemot en så kallad Alliansregering. Snarare det motsatta för att gå mer mot ”mitten” som de säger och det talar för att de kommer att driva frågor som lockar S-väljare som karensavdrag och tandvårdsreform. Kanske till och med en miljardärsskatt”. Syftet är, enligt Olofsson, att ”äta upp” S och ”locka deras väljare”. ”S är det parti som SD gillar allra minst och där SD:s långsiktiga mål har varit att försvaga det partiet. Så att en ny Alliansregering skulle kunna lita på stöd från SD tror jag inte på. SD har partiegoistiska ambitioner, inte ambitionen att göra Sverige bättre.”

articles.title: Teorin: Då kan SD och S göra upp
articles.summary: Genom att ställa sig utanför en regering kan SD få större frihet att göra upp med både höger- och vänstersidan i enskilda frågor. Det menar Carl Eos Richard Sörman och Chang Frick.
articles.body_text: SD:s besked att de släpper kravet på ministerposter öppnar för nya politiska samarbeten – bland annat med Socialdemokraterna. Det tror de SD-nära debattörerna Carl Eos och Richard Sörman. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Sverigedemokraterna har släppt kraven på ministerposter. Beskedet kan öppna upp för att göra upp med Socialdemokrater i vissa frågor, exempelvis tandvården tror Carl Eos och Richard Sörman. Genom att ställa sig utanför en regering kan SD få större frihet att göra upp med både höger- och vänstersidan i enskilda frågor. Det menar flera SD-nära debattörer som på lördagsmorgonen diskuterade partiledarens nya besked i P1 Morgon. – Det öppnar ju kanske för första gången någonsin också för SD att göra upp med Socialdemokraterna, säger Carl Eos, vid den konservativa tankesmedjan Oikos. Han pekar ut tandvårdsreformen som en möjlig fråga där partierna skulle kunna hitta gemensam mark. Både SD och Socialdemokraterna har drivit frågan om billigare tandvård, och enligt Eos skulle SD kunna söka stöd hos S i den frågan samtidigt som partiet förhandlar med en borgerlig regering i andra frågor. Även Richard Sörman, politisk redaktör på den SD-nära kanalen Riks, ser möjligheter till uppgörelser över blockgränsen. Han tror att Socialdemokraterna kan ha intresse av att ett samarbete med SD i vissa frågor för att försvåra för en borgerlig regering. Detta trots att Socialdemokraterna gjort klart att man kan regera med alla partier – utom just SD. – Inte i formellt samarbete, men ändå i några frågor att man går ihop med Sverigedemokraterna . Vilket man ju tidigare har sagt att man aldrig skulle göra naturligtvis, men Socialdemokraterna kommer ju ha ett intresse av att visa att den här borgerliga regeringen är bräcklig, säger han i P1. På fredagen meddelade Jimmie Åkesson att SD inte längre kräver ministerposter för att släppa fram en ny regering. Partiet är i stället berett att tolerera en regering bestående av M, KD, L och C med Ulf Kristersson som statsminister.

articles.title: Synen som får möss att bli redo att slåss
articles.summary: Möss som ser på när andra möss slåss beter sig som om de själva har varit med och bråkat. Deras hjärnor påverkas också, bara genom att titta på, visar en ny studie.
articles.body_text: Möss som ser på när andra möss slåss beter sig som om de själva har varit med och bråkat. Deras hjärnor påverkas också, bara genom att titta på, visar en ny studie. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I en studie delades ett antal hanmöss in i tre grupper. En grupp kallades för slagskämpar, en för åskådare och en för nybörjarslagskämpar. Mössen fick sedan under åtta dagar delta i tre olika försök på tio minuter vardera. ”Slagskämparna” fick slåss med en underlägsen, mindre mus. ”Åskådarmössen” satt på en upphöjd plats med en genomskinlig barriär och tittade på när de andra slogs. ”Nybörjarmössen” fick slåss med en leksaksmus, men såg inga andra slagsmål. Den nionde dagen ställdes samtliga möss mot en svårslagen motståndare. De möss som slagits mot riktiga möss var bra på att fajtas, men de som bara tittat på var nästan lika bra. De som mött en leksaksmus var däremot inte lika benägna att slåss. Både slagskämparna och åskådarna tillbringade också mindre tid med ryggen vänd mot sina motståndare. Däremot gick åskådarna inte till attack i större utsträckning, vilket forskarna tolkar som att de inte blev mer aggressiva av att titta på våld. När forskarna undersökte mössens hjärnor såg de att de som bara tittat på uppvisade förändringar hjärnan som liknande dem i hjärnorna hos slagskämparna. Ytterligare en upptäckt i studien, som publiceras i Nature, var att mössen inte verkade kunna slita blicken från ett pågående slagsmål. Det gäller även för apor och oss människor, har tidigare studier visat. Eftersom det rör sig om en musstudie går det inte att översätta resultaten direkt till människor, men forskarna skriver att upptäckterna kan ge ledtrådar om hur exponering för våldsamma upplevelser formar människors sätt att reagera på hot.
